verses.1:
This is the burden against Tyre:
 Wail, O ships of Tarshish, + 23:1 Or Wail, O fleet of trading ships ; also in verse 14 
 for Tyre is laid waste,
 without house or harbor.
 Word has reached them
 from the land of Cyprus. + 23:1 Hebrew Kittim ; also in verse 12
verses.2:
Be silent, O dwellers of the coastland,
 you merchants of Sidon,
 whose traders have crossed the sea. + 23:2 DSS and LXX; MT whom the seafarers have enriched
verses.4:
Be ashamed, O Sidon, the stronghold of the sea,
 for the sea has spoken:
 “I have not been in labor
 or given birth.
 I have not raised young men
 or brought up young women.”
verses.5:
When the report reaches Egypt,
 they will writhe in agony over the news of Tyre.
verses.6:
Cross over to Tarshish;
 wail, O inhabitants of the coastland!
verses.7:
Is this your jubilant city,
 whose origin is from antiquity,
 whose feet have taken her
 to settle far away?
verses.8:
Who planned this against Tyre,
 the bestower of crowns,
 whose traders are princes,
 whose merchants are renowned on the earth?
verses.9:
The LORD of Hosts planned it,
 to defile all its glorious beauty,
 to disgrace all the renowned of the earth.
verses.10:
Cultivate + 23:10 DSS and some LXX manuscripts; MT Overflow your land like the Nile, O Daughter of Tarshish;
 there is no longer a harbor.
verses.11:
The LORD has stretched out His hand over the sea;
 He has made kingdoms tremble.
 He has given a command
 that the strongholds of Canaan be destroyed.
verses.12:
He said, “You shall rejoice no more,
 O oppressed Virgin Daughter of Sidon.
 Get up and cross over to Cyprus—
 even there you will find no rest.”
verses.13:
Look at the land of the Chaldeans + 23:13 That is, the Babylonians —
 a people now of no account.
 The Assyrians destined it for the desert creatures;
 they set up their siege towers and stripped its palaces.
 They brought it to ruin.
verses.14:
Wail, O ships of Tarshish,
 for your harbor has been destroyed!
verses.15: At that time Tyre will be forgotten for seventy years— the span of a king’s life. But at the end of seventy years, it will happen to Tyre as in the song of the harlot:
verses.16:
“Take up your harp,
 stroll through the city,
 O forgotten harlot.
 Make sweet melody,
 sing many a song,
 so you will be remembered.”
verses.17: And at the end of seventy years, the LORD will restore Tyre. Then she will return to hire as a prostitute and sell herself to all the kingdoms on the face of the earth.
verses.18: Yet her profits and wages will be set apart to the LORD; they will not be stored or saved, for her profit will go to those who live before the LORD, for abundant food and fine clothing.
